front.title: Context and Correlation Management Architecture for Distributed Agentic Activities

abstract.t:
Agentic applications increasingly distribute objectives across autonomous agents, tools, and services operating across different protocols and administrative domains. A single Activity may involve multiple independently maintained Dialogs, Tasks, Events, and Resources, spanning different modalities and extended periods of time.
Existing protocols provide identifiers and context-management mechanisms for their own interactions, but these do not necessarily support correlation across Dialogs, protocols, and administrative boundaries, particularly as interactions evolve, branch, or resume over time.
This document defines a context-and-correlation architecture based on Activities, Dialogs, Tasks, Resources, and typed Relationships. It describes how management and correlation metadata can be maintained and selectively propagated to preserve coherent context across distributed interactions, while allowing participants to determine the scope of correlations they share and manage.
